# SWK Properties

> SWK Properties LLC is a RERA-licensed Dubai real estate brokerage (ORN 51517) on Sheikh Zayed Road. It advises buyers, investors, tenants and landlords on off-plan launches, ready homes, leasing and property management across the UAE.

## Guides
- [All guides](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides)
- [Complete Guide to Buying Property in Dubai (Ready & Off-Plan)](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/buying): Both UAE residents and non-resident foreign nationals can purchase 100% freehold property in designated Dubai zones. On top of the agreed purchase price, buyers should budget approximately 6% to 7.5% in upfront transaction costs—primarily the 4% Dubai Land Department (DLD) transfer/Oqood fee, DLD Trustee fee (AED 2,100–4,200), Title Deed issuance (AED 580), and 2% brokerage commission (+5% VAT) on secondary resales.
- [Complete Guide to Renting Property in Dubai (Ejari, Cheques & Tenant Rights)](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/renting): Residential leases in Dubai are governed by RERA and must be registered in the official Ejari system. Tenants typically pay annual rent in 1 to 4 post-dated cheques, provide a refundable security deposit (5% unfurnished or 10% furnished), pay a 5% agency commission (+5% VAT), and activate DEWA utilities (AED 2,000 refundable deposit for apartments or AED 4,000 for villas).
- [Complete Guide to Selling Your Dubai Property](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/selling): To legally market and sell a property in Dubai, the registered owner must sign RERA Form A with a licensed brokerage (maximum 3 brokerages at any one time) via the Dubai REST app so a DLD Trakheesi marketing permit and Madmoun QR code can be issued. Sellers typically pay the Developer NOC fee (AED 500–5,000), mortgage early-settlement fee if financed (up to 1% capped at AED 10,000), and agreed agency fee.
- [Dubai Real Estate Investment Guide (Net Yields, Payment Plans & Risk Controls)](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/investing): Dubai residential real estate offers 0% annual property tax and 0% personal rental income tax in the UAE, with the UAE Dirham pegged to the US Dollar at 3.6725 AED/USD since 1997. However, disciplined investors always calculate Net Yield rather than Gross Yield—deducting annual RERA Mollak service charges, maintenance reserves, leasing fees, and vacancy buffers—and verify developer escrow compliance before committing capital.

## Services
- [Off-plan advisory](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/off-plan-advisory): Off-plan means buying a home before it is finished, usually in stages tied to construction. It can put you into a community early on a structured payment plan, but it also means you carry delivery risk. We help you read a launch the way a lender would: who is building it, what has been delivered before, where your money sits, and what happens if dates slip.
- [Buying & selling ready property](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/secondary-market): Ready property means you can see what you are buying, check the building, and often move or rent within weeks. Whether you are buying or selling, our job is to price realistically, negotiate on evidence, and keep the transfer moving through the Dubai Land Department without surprises.
- [Leasing & rental](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/leasing-rental): Most Dubai tenancies are yearly and registered through Ejari. For tenants we match you to buildings by commute, budget and lifestyle. For landlords we find a reliable tenant, set a sensible rent, and make sure the paperwork is right from day one.
- [Investment advisory](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/investment-advisory): A good investment starts with a clear objective: monthly income, long-term growth or residency. We model each option on realistic rents, service charges and holding costs, and we tell you when a launch does not stack up.
- [Property management](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/property-management): If you own in Dubai but do not live here, or simply do not want to chase maintenance and cheques, we manage the tenancy for you and report clearly on what happened and what it cost.
- [Mortgage assistance](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/mortgage-assistance): Mortgage rules for UAE residents and non-residents differ on loan-to-value and documentation. We introduce you to lending partners, compare terms side by side, and keep the application moving so it does not hold up your purchase.
- [Legal & documentation](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/legal-documentation): The paperwork behind a Dubai purchase is straightforward when someone explains it in order. We coordinate with legal partners so you understand what you sign and when.
- [Interior & fit-out](https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/interior-fitout): A unit that is furnished well rents faster and holds its value. We scope the work against your budget and the likely tenant, then manage the contractors so you are not on site.

# Frequently asked questions

## Can foreigners buy property in Dubai?

Yes. Non-UAE nationals can purchase freehold property with full ownership rights in designated freehold areas such as Downtown Dubai, Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, Business Bay, and Dubai Hills Estate. SWK Properties only lists freehold-eligible listings for international buyers.

## What are the total costs involved in buying a property?

Beyond the purchase price, budget for a 4% Dubai Land Department (DLD) transfer fee, an AED 4,200 DLD admin fee, a 2% agency commission, and (for mortgaged purchases) a 0.25% mortgage registration fee plus bank arrangement fees. Our team provides a full cost breakdown before you commit.

## How do off-plan payment plans typically work?

Most developers offer staged plans such as 60/40 or 70/30 (percentage due during construction vs. on handover), or post-handover plans extending payments over 1-5 years after completion. Exact structures vary by project — each listing page shows the specific plan.

## Does buying property qualify me for a UAE Golden Visa?

Yes. A property investment of AED 2 million or more (subject to current immigration rules) can qualify you for a 10-year renewable UAE Golden Visa, extendable to spouse and children. Our legal partners handle the eligibility check and application.

## What financing options are available for overseas buyers?

Non-resident buyers can typically secure UAE mortgages of up to 50% loan-to-value, while UAE residents can access up to 80% LTV on their first property. We work with multiple banks to compare rates — try our mortgage calculator for an instant estimate.

## What ongoing costs should I expect as an owner?

Annual service charges (community/building maintenance, billed per sqft), a 5% housing fee on rented properties (charged via DEWA bills), and — if you let the property — a standard property management fee, typically 5-8% of annual rent.

## How is rental ROI calculated on your listings?

Each listing's ROI% is estimated using current market rents for comparable units in the same building or community, divided by the purchase price, net of an assumed service charge and vacancy allowance. Figures are indicative — our advisors can prepare a tailored projection.

## Can SWK Properties manage my property after I buy it?

Yes. Our property management team handles tenant sourcing, Ejari registration, rent collection, maintenance coordination, and renewals, so overseas owners can hold a fully hands-off investment.

# Complete Guide to Buying Property in Dubai (Ready & Off-Plan)

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/buying (updated 2026-11-01)

Both UAE residents and non-resident foreign nationals can purchase 100% freehold property in designated Dubai zones. On top of the agreed purchase price, buyers should budget approximately 6% to 7.5% in upfront transaction costs—primarily the 4% Dubai Land Department (DLD) transfer/Oqood fee, DLD Trustee fee (AED 2,100–4,200), Title Deed issuance (AED 580), and 2% brokerage commission (+5% VAT) on secondary resales.

Key takeaways:
- 1. Define Objective, Freehold Zone & Total Cost Envelope: Decide whether you are acquiring for personal occupation, long-term rental yield, or milestone capital appreciation, and confirm whether you are purchasing in cash or with UAE mortgage finance.
- 2. Choosing Between Off-Plan and Ready Secondary Market: Off-plan purchases are booked directly with the developer via a Sales & Purchase Agreement (SPA) and a DLD RERA Escrow Account, whereas ready secondary purchases use RERA Form F (Contract F) via the Dubai REST app.
- 3. Valuation, NOC & DLD Registration Trustee Transfer: Once the Developer NOC is issued (and bank final offer letter is signed if financed), buyer, seller, and licensed RERA broker meet at an authorised DLD Registration Trustee office.

## 1. Define Objective, Freehold Zone & Total Cost Envelope

Decide whether you are acquiring for personal occupation, long-term rental yield, or milestone capital appreciation, and confirm whether you are purchasing in cash or with UAE mortgage finance.

Decide whether you are acquiring for personal occupation, long-term rental yield, or milestone capital appreciation, and confirm whether you are purchasing in cash or with UAE mortgage finance.
- Non-residents can purchase freehold properties in designated zones including Downtown Dubai, Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, Business Bay, Dubai Hills Estate, JVC, and Dubai Creek Harbour.
- Mortgage buyers must obtain bank pre-approval before signing RERA Form F (MOU) to avoid forfeiting the 10% security deposit cheque.
- Factor annual RERA Mollak service charges (typically AED 4–7/sq ft for villas/townhouses and AED 14–32/sq ft for apartments) into your holding budget.

## 2. Choosing Between Off-Plan and Ready Secondary Market

Off-plan purchases are booked directly with the developer via a Sales & Purchase Agreement (SPA) and a DLD RERA Escrow Account, whereas ready secondary purchases use RERA Form F (Contract F) via the Dubai REST app.

Off-plan purchases are booked directly with the developer via a Sales & Purchase Agreement (SPA) and a DLD RERA Escrow Account, whereas ready secondary purchases use RERA Form F (Contract F) via the Dubai REST app.
- Off-plan: Typically 10%–20% down payment + 4% DLD Oqood registration fee, followed by construction-linked or milestone payments into a project-specific RERA escrow bank account.
- Ready Secondary: Buyer and seller sign RERA Form F electronically; buyer lodges a 10% security deposit cheque held by the brokerage trust/trustee until transfer.
- Developer NOC: For ready properties, the seller applies for a Developer No Objection Certificate (AED 500–5,000) confirming all service charges are settled.

## 3. Valuation, NOC & DLD Registration Trustee Transfer

Once the Developer NOC is issued (and bank final offer letter is signed if financed), buyer, seller, and licensed RERA broker meet at an authorised DLD Registration Trustee office.

Once the Developer NOC is issued (and bank final offer letter is signed if financed), buyer, seller, and licensed RERA broker meet at an authorised DLD Registration Trustee office.
- Settlement is executed via UAE Central Bank Manager's Cheques (or DLD e-Payment / escrow settlement).
- The new Title Deed (for ready homes) or Oqood registration (for off-plan) is issued digitally on the same day with a verifiable QR code.
- Properties valued at AED 2,000,000 or above qualify the title holder to apply for the 10-year UAE Golden Visa subject to DLD and ICP rules.

### Can a non-resident buy property in Dubai remotely?

Yes. Both off-plan SPAs and secondary market transfers can be completed remotely using digital verification via the Dubai REST app or a notarised Power of Attorney (POA) attested for use in the UAE.

### How do I verify that a Dubai property listing is genuine?

Check the listing's DLD Trakheesi Permit Number and scan the Madmoun QR code or verify the brokerage's RERA ORN (SWK Properties ORN: 51517) on dubailand.gov.ae.

# Complete Guide to Renting Property in Dubai (Ejari, Cheques & Tenant Rights)

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/renting (updated 2026-11-01)

Residential leases in Dubai are governed by RERA and must be registered in the official Ejari system. Tenants typically pay annual rent in 1 to 4 post-dated cheques, provide a refundable security deposit (5% unfurnished or 10% furnished), pay a 5% agency commission (+5% VAT), and activate DEWA utilities (AED 2,000 refundable deposit for apartments or AED 4,000 for villas).

Key takeaways:
- 1. Required Documents & Rental Payment Structure: To sign an annual residential lease and register Ejari, tenants need valid UAE residency documentation and a UAE bank chequebook (or approved corporate/manager's transfer).
- 2. Ejari Registration, DEWA, Chiller & Move-In Permit: Once the RERA Unified Tenancy Contract is signed by both parties, Ejari registration automatically triggers your DEWA water and electricity account.
- 3. Lease Renewals, 90-Day Notice & RERA Smart Rental Index: Dubai tenancy law protects both tenants and landlords with clear notice rules and regulated renewal caps.

## 1. Required Documents & Rental Payment Structure

To sign an annual residential lease and register Ejari, tenants need valid UAE residency documentation and a UAE bank chequebook (or approved corporate/manager's transfer).

To sign an annual residential lease and register Ejari, tenants need valid UAE residency documentation and a UAE bank chequebook (or approved corporate/manager's transfer).
- Documents required: Passport copy, UAE Residence Visa, Emirates ID, and landlord's Title Deed + passport copy.
- Rent payment: Negotiated between 1 cheque (often commands the strongest rental rate) and 2, 4, or 6 cheques.
- Security deposit: 5% of annual rent for unfurnished properties or 10% for furnished properties, held by the landlord and refundable at checkout.

## 2. Ejari Registration, DEWA, Chiller & Move-In Permit

Once the RERA Unified Tenancy Contract is signed by both parties, Ejari registration automatically triggers your DEWA water and electricity account.

Once the RERA Unified Tenancy Contract is signed by both parties, Ejari registration automatically triggers your DEWA water and electricity account.
- Ejari registration: Completed online via Dubai REST (~AED 175) or at an Ejari typing centre (~AED 220).
- DEWA security deposit: AED 2,000 for apartments or AED 4,000 for villas (refundable upon move-out) plus AED 130 activation fee.
- District cooling (Chiller): Confirm before signing whether the building is 'Chiller-Free' (covered by landlord's service charges) or billed separately via Empower/Emicool/Tabreed.
- Dubai Municipality Housing Fee: 5% of annual rent, billed automatically in 12 monthly instalments on your DEWA bill.

## 3. Lease Renewals, 90-Day Notice & RERA Smart Rental Index

Dubai tenancy law protects both tenants and landlords with clear notice rules and regulated renewal caps.

Dubai tenancy law protects both tenants and landlords with clear notice rules and regulated renewal caps.
- Any change to rent or contract terms at renewal requires at least 90 days' written notice prior to lease expiry.
- Permissible rent increases at renewal are benchmarked strictly against the official DLD / RERA Smart Rental Index.
- Maintenance responsibility: Typically, minor wear-and-tear under AED 500–1,000 is borne by the tenant, while major MEP/structural repairs are borne by the landlord (check the addendum).

### Can I rent a long-term apartment in Dubai before my Emirates ID is issued?

An Emirates ID (or official Emirates ID application receipt alongside residency processing) is required to register Ejari. If your visa is still in progress, SWK can arrange DTCM-licensed monthly residences until your Emirates ID is ready.

# Complete Guide to Selling Your Dubai Property

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/selling (updated 2026-11-01)

To legally market and sell a property in Dubai, the registered owner must sign RERA Form A with a licensed brokerage (maximum 3 brokerages at any one time) via the Dubai REST app so a DLD Trakheesi marketing permit and Madmoun QR code can be issued. Sellers typically pay the Developer NOC fee (AED 500–5,000), mortgage early-settlement fee if financed (up to 1% capped at AED 10,000), and agreed agency fee.

Key takeaways:
- 1. Data-Backed Valuation & Signing RERA Form A: Overpricing stalls listings in Dubai because portals display historical DLD transaction prices openly. We price properties using verified DLD transfers from the past 90 days.
- 2. Selling a Tenanted vs Vacant Property: Vacant-on-transfer homes appeal to both end-users and investors, while tenanted homes provide immediate day-one rental cash flow.
- 3. Form F, Liability Letter (if Mortgaged), Developer NOC & Transfer: A cash sale typically completes in 2 to 3 weeks; a sale involving a seller's mortgage clearance and/or buyer's mortgage typically takes 4 to 7 weeks.

## 1. Data-Backed Valuation & Signing RERA Form A

Overpricing stalls listings in Dubai because portals display historical DLD transaction prices openly. We price properties using verified DLD transfers from the past 90 days.

Overpricing stalls listings in Dubai because portals display historical DLD transaction prices openly. We price properties using verified DLD transfers from the past 90 days.
- Required seller documents: Title Deed (or Oqood for off-plan resale), valid Passport, Emirates ID (if resident), and latest service-charge statement.
- RERA Form A is generated digitally and approved by the owner via UAE Pass or Dubai REST OTP, generating the official Trakheesi permit and Madmoun QR code.
- Under DLD regulations, maximum 3 Form A permits can be active for the same unit simultaneously.

## 2. Selling a Tenanted vs Vacant Property

Vacant-on-transfer homes appeal to both end-users and investors, while tenanted homes provide immediate day-one rental cash flow.

Vacant-on-transfer homes appeal to both end-users and investors, while tenanted homes provide immediate day-one rental cash flow.
- If selling to an end-user who requires vacant possession from an existing tenant, Dubai law requires a 12-month eviction notice served via Notary Public or registered post.
- If selling with an active tenant in place, the security deposit and pro-rata rent cheque are reconciled on the settlement statement at DLD transfer.

## 3. Form F, Liability Letter (if Mortgaged), Developer NOC & Transfer

A cash sale typically completes in 2 to 3 weeks; a sale involving a seller's mortgage clearance and/or buyer's mortgage typically takes 4 to 7 weeks.

A cash sale typically completes in 2 to 3 weeks; a sale involving a seller's mortgage clearance and/or buyer's mortgage typically takes 4 to 7 weeks.
- If the property has an existing mortgage, the seller requests a Bank Liability Letter (~7–14 working days) and the buyer/buyer's bank settles the outstanding balance prior to NOC.
- Developer NOC is issued once service charges are paid up to the transfer date (excess service charges paid in advance are reimbursed pro-rata by the buyer).

### Can I sell an off-plan property before handover in Dubai?

Yes, once you have paid the developer's minimum resale threshold (typically 30% to 40% of the SPA price depending on the developer) and obtained the developer's NOC.

# Dubai Real Estate Investment Guide (Net Yields, Payment Plans & Risk Controls)

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/guides/investing (updated 2026-11-01)

Dubai residential real estate offers 0% annual property tax and 0% personal rental income tax in the UAE, with the UAE Dirham pegged to the US Dollar at 3.6725 AED/USD since 1997. However, disciplined investors always calculate Net Yield rather than Gross Yield—deducting annual RERA Mollak service charges, maintenance reserves, leasing fees, and vacancy buffers—and verify developer escrow compliance before committing capital.

Key takeaways:
- 1. Calculating True Net Yield (Not Headline Gross Yield): Headline gross yield is Annual Rent ÷ Purchase Price. True net yield deducts all upfront acquisition costs (DLD 4% + fees) and annual operating expenses.
- 2. Off-Plan Investment Due Diligence & Escrow Rules: Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 mandates that every off-plan project have a dedicated DLD project escrow account where buyer instalments are released only against certified construction milestones.
- 3. 10-Year UAE Golden Visa & Overseas Investor Structuring: Property investors acquiring AED 2,000,000 or more in Dubai real estate (ready or eligible off-plan) can apply for the renewable 10-year UAE residency visa.

## 1. Calculating True Net Yield (Not Headline Gross Yield)

Headline gross yield is Annual Rent ÷ Purchase Price. True net yield deducts all upfront acquisition costs (DLD 4% + fees) and annual operating expenses.

Headline gross yield is Annual Rent ÷ Purchase Price. True net yield deducts all upfront acquisition costs (DLD 4% + fees) and annual operating expenses.
- Formula: Net Yield (%) = (Annual Gross Rent − Annual Service Charges − Maintenance/Management Reserve) ÷ (Purchase Price + DLD & Acquisition Costs) × 100.
- Mid-market communities (such as JVC and Business Bay studios/1BRs) often produce higher percentage net yields, whereas prime waterfront and villa communities (Palm Jumeirah, Downtown Dubai, Dubai Hills Estate) historically exhibit stronger capital liquidity and lower tenant turnover.
- Never rely on 'guaranteed return' marketing without inspecting who underwrites the guarantee and whether the purchase price was inflated to fund it.

## 2. Off-Plan Investment Due Diligence & Escrow Rules

Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 mandates that every off-plan project have a dedicated DLD project escrow account where buyer instalments are released only against certified construction milestones.

Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007 mandates that every off-plan project have a dedicated DLD project escrow account where buyer instalments are released only against certified construction milestones.
- Verify the project number and escrow account bank on the Dubai Land Department (dubailand.gov.ae) or Dubai REST app before transferring funds.
- Assess the developer's historical handover record across previous cycles, not just their brochure renders.
- Check the minimum payment threshold required by the developer if you plan to exit (assign/resell) before completion.

## 3. 10-Year UAE Golden Visa & Overseas Investor Structuring

Property investors acquiring AED 2,000,000 or more in Dubai real estate (ready or eligible off-plan) can apply for the renewable 10-year UAE residency visa.

Property investors acquiring AED 2,000,000 or more in Dubai real estate (ready or eligible off-plan) can apply for the renewable 10-year UAE residency visa.
- Multiple properties in the investor's name can be combined to reach the AED 2,000,000 threshold.
- Mortgaged properties are eligible subject to the current DLD / ICP equity and bank NOC rules.
- Because the UAE Dirham (AED) is pegged to the USD at 3.6725, USD-linked investors face zero FX volatility between AED and USD.

### Are rental income or capital gains taxed in Dubai?

For individual private property owners in the UAE, there is currently no personal income tax on residential rental income and no capital gains tax on property resales. Overseas investors should always consult a tax advisor in their country of tax residence regarding foreign-source income rules.

# Off-plan advisory

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/off-plan-advisory

Off-plan means buying a home before it is finished, usually in stages tied to construction. It can put you into a community early on a structured payment plan, but it also means you carry delivery risk. We help you read a launch the way a lender would: who is building it, what has been delivered before, where your money sits, and what happens if dates slip.

### Is off-plan property in Dubai safe?

Dubai regulates off-plan sales through RERA project registration and escrow accounts that hold buyer payments. That reduces risk but does not remove it. We still check the developer's delivered projects and confirm the project is registered before you pay.

### What is Oqood?

Oqood is the Dubai Land Department's registration of an off-plan sale. It records your interest in the unit until the Title Deed is issued at handover.

### Can I resell before handover?

Often yes, once a minimum percentage of the price has been paid and the developer issues a no-objection certificate, but rules differ by developer. We check the resale terms in the SPA before you reserve.

# Buying & selling ready property

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/secondary-market

Ready property means you can see what you are buying, check the building, and often move or rent within weeks. Whether you are buying or selling, our job is to price realistically, negotiate on evidence, and keep the transfer moving through the Dubai Land Department without surprises.

### What are the total costs of buying a ready property in Dubai?

Besides the purchase price, expect the 4% DLD transfer fee, a AED 4,200 DLD admin fee, a 2% agency commission, and, if you take a mortgage, bank arrangement and valuation fees.

### How long does a resale take?

A cash purchase can transfer in around two to four weeks once documents are ready. A mortgage purchase takes longer because of valuation and bank approvals.

### Can foreigners buy ready property in Dubai?

Yes, in designated freehold areas such as Downtown Dubai, Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, Business Bay and Dubai Hills Estate. Ownership is full freehold.

# Leasing & rental

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/leasing-rental

Most Dubai tenancies are yearly and registered through Ejari. For tenants we match you to buildings by commute, budget and lifestyle. For landlords we find a reliable tenant, set a sensible rent, and make sure the paperwork is right from day one.

### What is Ejari?

Ejari is Dubai's tenancy contract registration system. It is needed for DEWA utilities, many visa applications and to enforce your rights as tenant or landlord.

### How are rents usually paid in Dubai?

Yearly rent is often paid in one to four instalments, commonly by post-dated cheque or bank transfer. The schedule is negotiated and written into the contract.

### Can I rent out a property while it has a mortgage?

Usually yes, but your lender may require consent. We check before listing.

# Investment advisory

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/investment-advisory

A good investment starts with a clear objective: monthly income, long-term growth or residency. We model each option on realistic rents, service charges and holding costs, and we tell you when a launch does not stack up.

### What rental yield can I expect in Dubai?

Gross yields vary widely by community, unit type and entry price. We show you net yield after service charges and vacancy for each shortlisted option instead of quoting a single market figure.

### Does property qualify me for a UAE Golden Visa?

Property investment can support a long-term residency visa if it meets the current minimum value and ownership conditions. Rules change, so we confirm the latest criteria with you before you buy.

# Property management

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/property-management

If you own in Dubai but do not live here, or simply do not want to chase maintenance and cheques, we manage the tenancy for you and report clearly on what happened and what it cost.

### Can I approve repairs before they are done?

Yes. Non-urgent repairs are quoted and need your approval. Emergencies are handled first and reported immediately.

# Mortgage assistance

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/mortgage-assistance

Mortgage rules for UAE residents and non-residents differ on loan-to-value and documentation. We introduce you to lending partners, compare terms side by side, and keep the application moving so it does not hold up your purchase.

### Can non-residents get a mortgage in the UAE?

Yes, though loan-to-value limits are usually lower than for residents and documentation is stricter. We map your options with lenders before you commit to a property.

# Legal & documentation

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/legal-documentation

The paperwork behind a Dubai purchase is straightforward when someone explains it in order. We coordinate with legal partners so you understand what you sign and when.

### Do I need to be in Dubai to buy?

No. With a power of attorney and remote document signing, many buyers complete without travelling. We tell you which steps do require presence.

# Interior & fit-out

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/services/interior-fitout

A unit that is furnished well rents faster and holds its value. We scope the work against your budget and the likely tenant, then manage the contractors so you are not on site.

### Does furnishing increase rent?

Furnished units often command a different rent range and can let faster, but the right choice depends on the building and tenant profile. We advise before you spend.

# Downtown Dubai

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/downtown-dubai

Downtown Dubai is the city's showpiece district, built around Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall and the Dubai Fountain. It is dense, walkable by Dubai standards and permanently busy, with a strong short-stay and long-term rental market.

Property types: Studios and one-bedroom apartments, Two to four bedroom apartments, Penthouses and branded residences
Best for: Investors seeking a prime address, Professionals who want to be central, Buyers who value brand and location
Transport: Burj Khalifa/Dubai Mall Metro Station on the Red Line; Direct access to Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road; Roughly 15 to 25 minutes to DXB airport by car outside peak hours (estimate)

# Dubai Marina

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/dubai-marina

Dubai Marina is a high-rise waterfront district around a man-made canal, with a long promenade, restaurants and direct access to the beach at JBR. It is a mature rental market popular with young professionals and families who want an active neighbourhood.

Property types: Studios to three-bedroom apartments, Penthouses, Waterfront and marina-view units
Best for: Renters and investors targeting professionals, Buyers who like waterfront living
Transport: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers metro stations on the Red Line; Dubai Tram along the Marina and JBR; Sheikh Zayed Road within a few minutes (estimate, traffic dependent)

# Palm Jumeirah

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/palm-jumeirah

Palm Jumeirah is the world-famous man-made island, with beachfront villas on the fronds, apartment buildings on the trunk and a growing set of branded residences. It is Dubai's most recognisable luxury address.

Property types: Frond villas, Apartments on the trunk and crescent, Branded residences and penthouses
Best for: Luxury buyers, Long-horizon investors, Families who want beach access
Transport: Palm Monorail connecting the trunk to the Gateway and Atlantis stations; Single main access road to the mainland, which can queue at peak times (estimate); Close to Al Sufouh and Sheikh Zayed Road

# Business Bay

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/business-bay

Business Bay is a central mixed-use district beside the Dubai Canal and a few minutes from Downtown. It mixes offices, apartments and hotels, and appeals to professionals who want to live close to work.

Property types: Studios and one-bedroom apartments, Two and three bedroom apartments, Serviced residences
Best for: Young professionals, Investors seeking central rental demand
Transport: Business Bay Metro Station on the Red Line; Close to Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road; Short drive to Downtown (estimate)

# Dubai Hills Estate

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/dubai-hills-estate

Dubai Hills Estate is a master-planned community around an 18-hole golf course, with parks, a mall, schools and a mix of apartments, townhouses and villas. It suits families who want green space close to the city.

Property types: Apartments, Townhouses, Villas and mansions
Best for: Families, Owner-occupiers, Buyers who want a master-planned address
Transport: Road access via Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Road; Metro is not on-site; most residents drive (estimate: 20 to 25 minutes to Downtown outside peak)

# Jumeirah Village Circle

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/jvc

Jumeirah Village Circle is a large, circular community in the middle of New Dubai with a broad mix of apartments and townhouses at more accessible prices. It is popular with first-time buyers and rental investors.

Property types: Studios and one to three bedroom apartments, Townhouses and villas, Serviced apartments
Best for: First-time buyers, Rental investors on a budget
Transport: Road access to Al Khail Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road; No metro on site (estimate: 20 to 30 minutes to Marina or Downtown, traffic dependent)

# Dubai Creek Harbour

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/dubai-creek-harbour

Dubai Creek Harbour is a waterfront masterplan beside Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary, planned around parks, a marina and a landmark observation tower. It is still maturing, with new phases launching regularly.

Property types: Apartments, Townhouses, Waterfront residences
Best for: Buyers who want waterfront and space, Long-term investors comfortable with a growing area
Transport: Road links to Ras Al Khor Road and Al Khail Road; Planned metro connection (check current status); Close to Downtown (estimate: 10 to 15 minutes outside peak)

# Sheikh Zayed Road

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/communities/sheikh-zayed-road

Sheikh Zayed Road is Dubai's business spine, lined with landmark towers, offices and hotels, with metro stops along its length. SWK's own office is here, at Al Saqr Business Tower.

Property types: Apartments in towers, Serviced residences, Commercial offices
Best for: Business owners, Investors in offices and small units
Transport: Multiple Red Line metro stations along the road; Direct highway links to Downtown, Marina and Abu Dhabi

# How to read a developer's track record before you reserve

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/read-a-developers-track-record (updated 2026-10-20)

Judge a developer by what it has already handed over, not by what it has launched. Visit a completed community, read the registered project details, and speak to residents before you reserve.

- Start with delivered communities, not the launch event: Ask for a list of completed projects and visit one on a weekday evening.
- Compare promised and actual handover: Find the original launch announcement for a past project and compare its stated completion window with the real handover.
- Check the registration and the paper trail: In Dubai, off-plan projects should be registered with the Dubai Land Department and carry a project registration number.
- Talk to owners, not only agents: Residents of a past project can tell you things a brochure cannot: how maintenance responds, how service charges have moved, and whether the facilities match the renders.

# Escrow, Oqood and the off-plan paper trail

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/escrow-oqood-and-the-offplan-paper-trail (updated 2026-10-14)

Buyer payments for registered off-plan projects in Dubai are meant to go into the project's escrow account, and the sale is recorded through the interim registration system known as Oqood. Keep every document and pay only into the account named in your contract.

- The escrow account: Dubai's regulations require developers of registered off-plan projects to hold buyer payments in a project-specific escrow account, from which funds are released against construction progress.
- Oqood: the interim registration: Off-plan sale contracts are recorded through an interim register at the Dubai Land Department, commonly called Oqood.
- The sale and purchase agreement: The agreement sets out the payment schedule, the handover window, what happens on delay and what you may and may not do before handover.
- What to keep: Keep the signed agreement, every payment receipt, the escrow account details, the registration certificate and every written exchange with the developer.

# Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Sharjah: choose the emirate before the project

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/dubai-abu-dhabi-or-sharjah (updated 2026-10-08)

Pick the emirate for your life and your goal first, then the developer and the project. Ownership rules, lifestyle and rental demand differ between Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.

- Ownership rules are set emirate by emirate: Property ownership for non-citizens depends on the emirate and on designated freehold or investment zones.
- Dubai: depth and choice: Dubai offers the largest range of developers, communities and resale activity.
- Abu Dhabi: master communities and calm: Aldar's island communities on Saadiyat, Yas and Fahid suit buyers who want a quieter, more planned environment and a capital-city setting.
- Sharjah: a different pace and a different entry point: Arada's Aljada and Masaar communities are changing how people look at Sharjah, as a place to live with a cultural core and calmer streets, within commuting distance of Dubai.

# Read a payment plan like a cash-flow schedule

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/payment-plans-as-cash-flow (updated 2026-10-01)

Convert any payment plan into a month-by-month calendar in your own currency, then add the costs the plan does not show. If the calendar looks tight in any single month, ask for a different structure or a different project.

- Know which type of plan you are looking at: Some plans tie instalments to construction milestones; others to fixed dates; some extend after handover.
- Build the calendar yourself: List every instalment with its date or trigger.
- Think in your own currency: The dirham is pegged to the US dollar, so exchange-rate risk for buyers paying from India, Pakistan, Russia or the UK sits in your home currency against the dollar.
- Ask what happens when plans slip: Find out how the contract treats a late payment, a handover delay and a request to change the schedule.

# Branded residences: what the name adds, and what it cannot

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/branded-residences-what-the-name-adds (updated 2026-09-24)

A brand name can bring design standards and hotel-grade service, but it does not remove the need to read the operating agreement, the service charges and the exit route.

- What the brand usually brings: Hospitality names such as Dorchester Collection, Four Seasons and Anantara typically bring a service model, concierge and design standards.
- What it does not change: The building still has to be well built, well managed and well located.
- Read the operating terms: Ask who runs the building, how long the brand licence lasts, what happens if the brand leaves, and how service charges are set.
- Think about the exit: A branded home may appeal to a narrower group of future buyers.

# Questions to ask at the sales gallery, and the answers that should worry you

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/questions-for-the-sales-gallery (updated 2026-09-17)

Bring a written list. Ask about registration, escrow, delivery history, service charges, and what is and is not included. Note who answers directly and who changes the subject.

- Is this project registered, and can I see the number?: A registered project has a number you can verify.
- Where do my payments go?: The answer should be the project's escrow account.
- What did you hand over last, and when did you promise it?: Compare the promised and actual dates.
- What is not in the model?: Show models often include finishes, furniture and views that are not in the standard unit.

# Buying from abroad: a checklist for non-resident buyers

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/buying-from-abroad-a-checklist (updated 2026-09-10)

Confirm your home-country rules for sending money abroad, line up your identification and source-of-funds paperwork, and appoint someone you trust to attend viewings and handover.

- Check the rules at home first: Many countries regulate how much money residents can send abroad and for what purpose.
- Prepare identity and source-of-funds documents: Developers, banks and the regulator will ask who you are and where the money comes from.
- Use the right payment channel: Pay by bank transfer to the named escrow account, from an account in your own name where possible.
- Appoint someone you trust: A family member or adviser who can attend viewings, sign for keys and inspect the handover can make remote buying far smoother.

# Off-plan or ready in Dubai? Start with the date you need the keys

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/off-plan-vs-ready-2026 (updated 2026-10-24)

An off-plan apartment and a ready apartment can share the same price and still ask very different things of your finances. Start with when you need the home, how much cash you can commit and what happens if your timetable changes.

- Put your own deadline first: If you need somewhere to live soon, begin with homes you can inspect and a realistic transfer timetable.
- Compare payments on a calendar: Write down every payment date, including the reservation, construction instalments and any amount due at handover.
- Check the project, then the paperwork: Dubai Land Department provides a project-status enquiry through Dubai REST.
- Look at what you can actually inspect: A finished home lets you examine light, noise, room dimensions and common areas.

# Dubai property Golden Visa: questions to settle before you buy

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/golden-visa-property-guide (updated 2026-10-24)

Dubai Land Department lists a property-investor route for a renewable ten-year residence permit with a qualifying purchase value of at least AED 2 million. That threshold is a starting point for an eligibility check, not a promise of approval for a particular purchase.

- Start with the authority’s current requirements: Use the official DLD investor service page as the starting point.
- If there is a mortgage, ask a precise question: DLD’s service information specifies a bank letter showing AED 2 million paid for a mortgaged property.
- Choose a home that also works without the visa: Think through location, condition, running costs and how long you expect to own the property.
- Prepare documents without sending them to strangers: Ask the official service channel for its current checklist and submit identity and ownership documents through that channel.

# Comparing Dubai rental yields: five neighbourhoods, one honest worksheet

Source: https://www.swkpropertiesuae.com/insights/best-communities-for-rental-yield (updated 2026-10-24)

There is no single rental yield for an entire Dubai neighbourhood. The purchase price, building costs, condition and rent actually achieved matter more than a headline league table. Compare individual units with the same worksheet before choosing an area.

- Use one definition of yield: For a simple gross yield, divide annual rent by purchase price and multiply by 100.
- Jumeirah Village Circle: compare the building: For a JVC shortlist, compare units with a similar size and layout rather than grouping every apartment under the community name.
- Business Bay and Dubai Marina: compare daily use: Look beyond proximity to a recognisable skyline.
- Dubai Hills and Dubai South: compare what is available now: When discussing these communities, distinguish existing amenities from future plans and measure the commute yourself.
